name: Brazil
headline: Brazil: +2.3% growth in 2025, 5.0% inflation, debt 93% of GDP
sections: Brazil is a $2.28 trillion economy (2025), the world's 12th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.3% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $23K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 11.8% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 5.0% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 9.3% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 6.0% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 14.0% (2025).
Gross government debt is 93% of GDP (2025), a elevated level. The general government balance is −7.4% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −2.9% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 35% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 3.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 105% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 76.0 years (2024). Population: 213.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
